newsitem.title: USA: US shares Japan concern on recent yen moves -- Rubin.
newsitem.headline: US shares Japan concern on recent yen moves -- Rubin.

text.p: The United States shares Japan's concern about the recent weakening of the yen, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said Thursday.
"We share the concern expressed by the Japanese authorities last night about recent movements in the yen because of the impact on Japan's external surplus," Rubin said in a statement.
A weaker yen makes Japanese products more competitive on world markets, tending to boost the country's trade surplus.

Rubin, who visited Tokyo last Friday, noted that Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto stated last week that Japan needs strong domestic demand-led economic growth and had to avoid a significant rise in its surplus.
"The challenge for Japan is how to achieve these objectives," Rubin said. He said that U.S. dollar policy is unchanged and that exchange rates over time reflect fundamentals.
"Our policy on the dollar is unchanged," Rubin said.
"Over time, exchange rates generally reflect fundamentals and the fundamentals of the U.S. economy have been relatively strong for the past four years," he added.
